div.p: El Kef is the capital of its eponymous Tunisian governorate. It is located in the northwestern part of the country in the Tunisian-Algerian border region. Though beyond Tunisia’s touristic regions, the small town provides interesting insights into Tunisia’s cultural and historical heritage.

figure.head: Researcher Franzi in front the Roman baths ruins
Flowers planted within the area of the Roman baths

div.p: Ruins of a Roman bath (ḥammām) evoke the country’s antique past, while the Kasbah (qaṣba), a fort with a view over the whole town, goes back to the time of Ottoman rule.

figure.head: View of the city from the the Kasbah
Guns of and view from the Kasbah

div.p: An old synagogue in the centre of El Kef as well as a Jewish and a Christian cemetery are indicators of the former times’ religious diversity.

figure.head: On the way to the Synagogue de la Ghriba
Entrance of the Synagogue de la Ghriba
Yard with Ruins of the Synagogue de la Ghriba
Inside the Synagogue de la Ghriba

div.p: In addition to the mosque, the mausoleum of the local saint Sidi Bou Makhlouf (Sīdi Bū Maxlūf) is one of the holy places people visit to the present.
While historical traces are omnipresent, professional graffiti arts embellish roads, paths and public places showing the modern side of El Kef.

figure.head: Graffiti of a dove by Wiss
Graffiti of old men playing basketball
Artist Wiss in front of his graffiti of an eye

div.p: Some Kefian artists even integrate the town’s past into their work, using El Kef’s former Latin name Sicca Veneria as a graffiti motif.
This dialect was linguistically investigated within the TUNOCENT project, which resulted in the following publication: Ritt-Benmimoun (2022)
